issues.description: The template Lecture class declares addGuestStudents with a different parameter list (addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, boolean validateInput)) than the method described in the problem statement and implemented in the solution (addGuestStudents(int)). This parameter mismatch will confuse students and prevent them from implementing or compiling the expected method signature from the specification and tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template method signature to match the specification and solution: replace public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, boolean validateInput) with public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) (leave method body as TODO). Alternatively, update the problem statement and solution to require the boolean parameter and adjust tests accordingly. Prefer matching the UML/spec (single int parameter).

issues.description: The template Lecture class declares addGuestStudents with a different signature (addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, boolean validateInput)) than the problem statement and the solution (addGuestStudents(int)). This mismatch in the method identifier/signature creates a mapping barrier: students reading the exercise expect to implement/use addGuestStudents(int) as specified in the UML and tasks, but the provided template method stub requires an extra boolean parameter. This can confuse students about the required API and lead to failing tests or incorrect implementations.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template method signature with the problem statement and solution by changing the template stub to: public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) { ... } (remove the boolean validateInput parameter). Ensure any placeholder comments reflect the intended single-parameter behavior.
